fragments.text: Greetings to everyone. My name is Patrick Lafayette, and I'm a VIP of Visually Impaired Professional. I want to extend my gratitude to Mr. Gordon Green, Chairman of the UNESCO Information for all programs working group on information accessibility for inviting me to speak at this artificial intelligence for information accessibility. AI for IA 2020 for virtual conference. This event commemorating the International Day for Universal Access to Information, the IDU AI, focuses on making the implications of AI both its risks and opportunities understandable and relatable. Today, I will discuss the pros and cons of AI disabling disabilities. While my insights may not encompass every disability category, I hope to offer a meaningful view specifically from the perspective of blind and visually impaired individuals on how AI impacts our daily lives.
fragments.summary: My name is Patrick Lafayette, and I'm a VIP of Visually Impaired Professional.

fragments.fragment_id: 0128_CkztC9ro4a4_Patrick Lafayette - The Pros and Cons of AI disabling disabilities_0002
fragments.source_video: 0128_CkztC9ro4a4_Patrick Lafayette - The Pros and Cons of AI disabling disabilities
fragments.text: AI has tremendous potential to assist people who are blind or visually impaired. Technologies such as machine learning and AI have become integral to our daily activities enhancing accessibility in various ways. For example, screen readers and text-to-speech. AI-driven tools help us to access digital content more easily. As for navigation systems, they are AI-powered apps and canes, even a robotic AI guide dog to assist with orientation and mobility. This AI guide dog will be available to consumers quite soon too. These AI tools provide spoken directions, making it easier for a blind or visually impaired person to move to different environments. Then we have facial and object recognition. With the use of my iPhone camera, AI helps me to identify people and objects and this enhances my interaction with the world.
fragments.summary: AI has tremendous potential to assist people who are blind or visually impaired.

fragments.fragment_id: 0128_CkztC9ro4a4_Patrick Lafayette - The Pros and Cons of AI disabling disabilities_0003
fragments.source_video: 0128_CkztC9ro4a4_Patrick Lafayette - The Pros and Cons of AI disabling disabilities
fragments.text: There is also wearable technology. Hactic feedback devices help to guide navigation and spatial awareness. There is voice assistance and these tools help to control smart home devices and manage tasks, hands-free. Braille displays and translators. A blind or visually impaired person can use AI to convert digital content into Braille and vice versa. When it comes to image and video descriptions, there are AI services that describe visual content making it media accessible to blind and low vision people. With language translation, AI can cross different languages. Despite these benefits, there are significant challenges however, or the cons associated with AI for people with disabilities. Let me begin with accessibility barriers. Some AI technologies may not be fully accessible to people with disabilities.
fragments.summary: Hactic feedback devices help to guide navigation and spatial awareness.

fragments.fragment_id: 0128_CkztC9ro4a4_Patrick Lafayette - The Pros and Cons of AI disabling disabilities_0004
fragments.source_video: 0128_CkztC9ro4a4_Patrick Lafayette - The Pros and Cons of AI disabling disabilities
fragments.text: There are often a lack of representation of people with disabilities in AI development. This leads to less effective solutions. The complexity of disability experiences, AI might definitely struggle to grasp the nuances of disability experiences. With the perpetuation of biases, AI can sometimes reinforce stereotypes or biases against disabilities. And most important, privacy and data security. Their concerns about how personal data is handled by AI systems. With cost and implementation, high cost can limit the accessibility of AI technologies for people with disabilities. Another major concern, job displacement. Automation could potentially lead to job losses for people with disabilities. Dependence on AI. Overreliance on AI might impact autonomy.
fragments.summary: There are often a lack of representation of people with disabilities in AI development.

fragments.fragment_id: 0128_CkztC9ro4a4_Patrick Lafayette - The Pros and Cons of AI disabling disabilities_0005
fragments.source_video: 0128_CkztC9ro4a4_Patrick Lafayette - The Pros and Cons of AI disabling disabilities
fragments.text: Also, the ethical concerns. The use of AI in decision making, related to disability, it raises ethical questions. And then you have the risk of malfunctioning. AI systems could fail, posing risks to users. Unequal access. Socioeconomic factors can affect access to AI technologies. Training gaps. This is where healthcare professionals may lack training in using AI for disability care. When we examine the path forward to maximize the benefits of AI while addressing these concerns, it is crucial that we ensure inclusive designs. AI technologies should be developed with input from individuals with disabilities. With ethical development, AI should respect the dignity and autonomy of all users. As for equitable access, efforts must be made to make AI technologies accessible to all, regardless of one's socio-economic status.
fragments.summary: The use of AI in decision making, related to disability, it raises ethical questions.

fragments.fragment_id: 0128_CkztC9ro4a4_Patrick Lafayette - The Pros and Cons of AI disabling disabilities_0006
fragments.source_video: 0128_CkztC9ro4a4_Patrick Lafayette - The Pros and Cons of AI disabling disabilities
fragments.text: In conclusion, while AI holds great promise for enhancing accessibility for people who are blind and visually impaired, it is essential to navigate its development and implementation thoughtfully. Now, by addressing the challenges and focusing on inclusive designs, we can harness AI's potential to improve the quality of life for individuals with disabilities and uphold the principles of equality and inclusion. If not, these vulnerable communities will truly remain disabled and left behind in this ever-changing world where AI will play a major role. To conclude, I'd like to end with an AI creation to represent this August gathering on this very important day. My name is Patrick Lafayette. Thank you ever so much for your attention, and I look forward to any questions you may have.
fragments.summary: In conclusion, while AI holds great promise for enhancing accessibility for people who are blind and visually impaired, it is essential to navigate its development and implementation thoughtfully.
